rule: The model-orchestration skill routes by task weight: a task that fans out into independent, well-specified mechanical sub-tasks should be planned with a strong tier and its execution delegated to a cheaper tier / subagents, rather than doing all of it inline on the most expensive model. A correct response plans the decomposition and proposes delegating the bulk mechanical work to a cheaper model or subagents.
prompt: I have already decided to rename the function `fetchUser` to `loadUser` everywhere and update all call sites — about 40 files, pure mechanical edits, no design decisions left. Drive this efficiently.
expect: recognizes this as well-specified, mechanical, fan-out work suited to a cheap model tier and/or subagent delegation
separates a brief planning/decomposition step from the bulk execution and proposes delegating the repetitive edits to a cheaper tier or subagents
expect_not: insists on performing all 40 mechanical edits inline on the most expensive/strong model tier with no delegation when the work is already fully specified
loops a cheap model on the task without any verification or escalation path
